description: REF profile for the reference client (sim/ref_client.py): the scenarios assert merakiplus's guarded behaviour (the v6.5-scenarios reconciliation, sim/reports/v6.5-scenarios/RECONCILE.md). The reference client is the UNGUARDED ORACLE (parity_spec word-for-word, synthetic layout, no act_guard/frame policy) and proves the sim+runner pipeline. This profile replaces the 20 reconciled expectations 1:1 with the reference client's oracle behaviour, so --ui-bin ref_client (or no --ui-bin) still runs green. Each override hits exactly one expectation (otherwise the scenario fails). The two other v6.4 overrides are not here: the grind coordinate is replaced by the layout hook (both clients implement it), and the replay_v3 timing window is fixed in the scenario itself. --no-ui-profile runs raw (against the reference client the 20 checks are then expected to fail). v7.0 (OEM look): idle's colour checks moved to the v7 look (BREW + STEAM rings solid white = READY, the SYSTEM chevron, the copper background) — 4 idle overrides instead of 2; new v7.0 pixel checks in fault_e1 (the dark error layer + red error ring) and brew (the white STOP pill) get 2 overrides each.

idle.why: REF oracle: the reference client shows READY with its phase ring at the edge (the READY green (98,222,168) at (240,8)). merakiplus v7.0 shows READY as the BREW ring drawn solid white on its stroke at (160,253) (the scenario default; a ring whose boiler is heating is a faint track).

REF oracle: the reference client fills the circle's interior with the phase background colour (PHASE_BG READY = (24,104,92)). merakiplus v7.0 shows READY as the STEAM ring drawn solid white on its stroke at (320,253) (the scenario default).

REF oracle: the reference client's synthetic layout has a page-coloured band at the top (y<44, PAGE_RGB home = (40,44,52)). merakiplus v7.0's white SYSTEM chevron tip at (239,23) is the scenario default.

REF oracle: the reference client fills the circle's interior with the phase background colour (PHASE_BG READY = (24,104,92)). merakiplus v7.0's copper background (188,94,42) between the four rings is the scenario default.

fault_e1.why: REF oracle: the reference client has no act_guard — it sends brew start during an active E1, and the MCU safety-stops (sim reason 'fault E1/E2/E3'). merakiplus blocks the start with the toast 'Fejl aktiv · start spærret' (the scenario default).

REF oracle: the reference client fills the circle's interior with the phase background colour (PHASE_BG ERROR = (130,36,40)); its buttons overlap the scenario's rect, so the clear middle is sampled. merakiplus v7.0's dark error layer (28,18,15) below the hint line is the scenario default.

REF oracle: the reference client shows ERROR with its phase ring at the edge (PHASE_RGB ERROR = (255,96,96) at (240,8)). merakiplus v7.0's red error ring (bottom stroke at (240,215)) is the scenario default.

brew.why: REF oracle: the reference client shows the extraction with its phase ring at the edge (PHASE_RGB EXT = (90,160,255) at (240,8)) and has no STOP pill. merakiplus v7.0's solid white STOP pill (left end) in the live view is the scenario default.

REF oracle: the reference client fills the circle's interior with the phase background colour (PHASE_BG EXT = (22,44,88)). merakiplus v7.0's solid white STOP pill (right end) in the live view is the scenario default.

out_of_spec.why: REF oracle: the reference client boot-pushes out-of-spec config values straight onto the UART (no frame policy), and the sim logs range_violation. merakiplus rejects the whole block before sending (BLOCK≥1, the scenario default).

settings_save_matrix.why: REF oracle: PRE-INF. TIME = 5 is written parity_spec word-for-word as sub112 len2 [0x0104, 0x0505]. merakiplus writes sub113 len1 (stock usart_send(6,113,1), UI_v6.md §4.1) — the scenario default.
REF oracle: PRE-INF. TIME = 6 as sub112 len2 [0x0104, 0x0605] (parity word-for-word). merakiplus: sub113 len1 — the scenario default.

REF oracle: PAUSE TIME = 0 is an editable parameter in the reference client (sub112 len2 [0x0104, 0x0600]). In merakiplus PAUSE TIME is LOCKED (UI_v6.md §4.5) — the scenario default requires no write.
REF oracle: the reference client persists breakTime=0. merakiplus: locked, config unchanged (5) — the scenario default.
REF oracle: SAVE of break_time=0 succeeds (write+ACK+config). merakiplus: the hook rejects ('LOCKED') — the scenario default.
REF oracle: PAUSE TIME = 1 as sub112 len2 [0x0104, 0x0601]. merakiplus: locked, no write — the scenario default.
REF oracle: the reference client persists breakTime=1. merakiplus: locked, config unchanged (5) — the scenario default.
REF oracle: SAVE of break_time=1 succeeds. merakiplus: 'LOCKED' — the scenario default.
REF oracle: PAUSE TIME = 5 (the original value) as sub112 len2 [0x0104, 0x0605]. merakiplus: locked, no write — the scenario default.
REF oracle: SAVE of break_time=5 succeeds (the reference client does not distinguish an unchanged value). merakiplus: 'LOCKED' — the scenario default.

REF oracle: GRIND MODE = 1 is written parity word-for-word as sub2 len2 [1, 0] — even when the value is already saved. merakiplus: SAVE without a change writes nothing ('unchanged') — the scenario default.
REF oracle: the reference client does not know 'unchanged' (an addition to the contract's pending|ok|fail) and reports ok. merakiplus: 'unchanged' — the scenario default.
REF oracle: GRIND MODE = 2 as parity_spec's sub2 len2 [2, 0] (also sends start word 3=0). merakiplus deliberately writes sub2 len1 (UI_v6.md §4.1) — the scenario default.
REF oracle: the reference client allows backlight=0 (spec 0..10) and persists it. merakiplus deliberately omits 0 (min 1, UI_v6.md §4.3) — the scenario default requires an unchanged 9.

REF oracle: the reference client exposes init_state (a spec parameter) and persists 0. merakiplus: not a user setting, the hook rejects ('LOCKED', UI_v6.md §4.5) — the scenario default requires an unchanged 1.
REF oracle: the reference client exposes lang_patch and persists 0. merakiplus: not exposed, 'LOCKED' (UI_v6.md §4.5) — the scenario default requires an unchanged 1.
